_note: D-RESTORE-WITH-NO-WAY-TO-SEE-WHAT-IS-RESTORABLE, the canon-rule family, through the real chat path. The rule is created AND archived in the seed, so the turn arrives holding no rule_id — which is the defect: the only way to hold one was to have written it down before archiving.

scenarios.prompt: Undo delete rule — I archived a canon rule by mistake, please restore it.
scenarios.prompt_source: composition_canon_rule_restore's OWN declared synonyms, verbatim: 'undo delete rule' + 'restore it' alongside 'canon rule'.
scenarios.approve_why: Tier A, and the target is the run's OWN throwaway book, provisioned and torn down. Legitimate under the standing rule: the write is the RESTORE this scenario exists to reach, and leaving it unapproved would measure whether the model reaches the card, not whether the chain works. Bounded by max_approvals.

seed.why: The rule must exist before it can be archived. Its id is captured by the harness for the next step and is NEVER given to the model.

🔴 ARCHIVED IN THE SEED, which is the whole point. A turn that archived the rule itself would still be holding the id; this defect is about a turn that arrives AFTER, when the only surface that could name the rule showed non-archived rows only.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM canon_rule WHERE project_id='{project_id}' AND is_archived
seed_assert.why: Exactly one ARCHIVED rule before the turn. If it were not archived the listing would show it anyway and the scenario would measure nothing; if it did not exist there would be nothing to restore.

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: the model asks the AUTHOR for a rule_id (the recorded failure shape for this family — 'I can't see it in the trash without an ID'), OR it invents a rule_id, OR it calls composition_list_canon_rules WITHOUT include_archived and then reports there is nothing to restore, OR the rule is restored with NO confirm card (Tier A). Store check: canon_rule stays at exactly 1 row for this project — a restore must never create a second rule.

ship_audit.gate: OWED — Tier A; the restore mutates author-declared canon.
ship_audit.absent_case: a rule_id that does not exist must be refused — not covered here.
ship_audit.idempotency: restoring an already-active rule must not duplicate it — not covered here.
ship_audit.tenancy: project-scoped; the listing is VIEW-gated on the book.

answer_expect.why: The rule's TEXT can only have come from the archived listing — it is not in the prompt. A reply that talks about restoring in the abstract proves nothing; naming the rule proves the model actually saw the archived row.
